source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus is the largest disclosed power block in Illinois, at 114 MW of published IT capacity across three facilities.

The 114 MW is a power envelope, not a machine count. Converting it to racks requires an assumed density that the operator does not publish, so any rack or accelerator figure is an inference, not a fact from the spec page. What the data does establish is scale: 450,000 square feet of technical space and three facility codes, CHI1 through CHI3, under one campus.

The state context matters more than the campus number. Six Illinois facilities publish any megawatt figure, totaling 236 MW, so Aurora alone is close to half of what the state has disclosed. The other 40 mapped Illinois facilities publish nothing. The ranking therefore measures disclosure, not buildout, and Illinois real capacity is larger than 236 MW.

What this does not tell a reader is whether the 114 MW is delivered and energized, who occupies the space, or what hardware runs there. The only certification listed is Green Globes, which speaks to environmental design and not to tenant or workload. The spec page carries no address or postal code, so siting within Aurora is not established. For AI specifically, the binding question is whether this power is available, and the data stops short of answering it.
